notes: Topre America is the Springfield subsidiary of Tokyo-listed Topre Corporation; the company profile lists 6,860 consolidated employees as of March 2026, and the Springfield plant alone had 920 Form 5500 participants in 2019 and 580 retained jobs. A grant-year (2018-2022) consolidated figure was not fetched, so the 5000+ bucket rests on the 2026 count.

Plymouth, Michigan defense and ag-track maker with more than 980 employees (Feb 2023 release) that bought Continental's St. Marys plant in Dec 2021 and committed 250 new jobs plus 450 retained. The EIN maps to CP Prime Holdings, L.P., a Form D filer c/o The Carlyle Group (sec.gov CIK 1837752), so the operating company is treated as the parent with Carlyle as private-equity owner.

Toledo-based nonprofit health system founded 1986; its own retirement plan had 16,527 participants in 2015 and 19,307 in 2019, and the 2018 HCR ManorCare acquisition pushed total headcount well above that. Grant was a Revitalization Grant and Loan for the downtown Toledo headquarters project (900 jobs retained).

Nanogate North America (Nanogate Jay Systems, the former Jay Plastics of Mansfield) was the US arm of Nanogate SE of Goettelborn, Germany, which had 1,209 employees in 2017 and about 400 in Mansfield; the $2 million JobsOhio grant funded a Mansfield R&D center announced April 2018. Nanogate SE filed for insolvency in June 2020 and its core business went to Techniplas in 2021, so ownership changed right at the end of the grant years.

SEQ matches the southeast quadrant of MLK Drive and Reading Road in Cincinnati, the 5.8-acre Uptown Gateway site developed by Cincinnati-based Terrex (founded 2014) with Messer Construction; the asterisk in JobsOhio's metrics marks it as a project entity. No source was found that names Uptown SEQ Holdings LLC's owner directly, and Terrex publishes no headcount, so parent and size are inferred.

emp_source: Form 5500 participants 5,777 (2019) for sponsor Swagelok Company; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swagelok
notes: Swagelok Manufacturing Company LLC is a unit of privately held Swagelok Company of Solon, founded in Cleveland in 1947, with over 5,700 associates; JobsOhio's own report shows 5,237 jobs retained on this grant. The company is private, so no SEC figure exists.

Address-named LLC for the former 500,000 sq ft retail site at 3251 Westerville Road, converted into a modular-home factory by Connect Housing Blocks, a subsidiary of Columbus developer Connect Realty (founder Brad DeHays), with a 300-job target. The factory was a startup at the 2023 grant, so the <100 bucket reflects the developer, not the planned jobs.

Plastilene Inc. is the first US operation of Bogota-based Grupo Plastilene, which runs plants in Colombia, Ecuador and Guatemala and committed 58 R&D jobs and about $41-48 million in Washington Court House. No source giving the group's worldwide headcount was found (company site, JobsOhio release, WOSU and Dayton Development Coalition checked), so the bucket is a guess for a multi-country packaging manufacturer.

parent: Orlando Baking Company (with developer Weston Inc.)
notes: Project Boron is the 156,000 sq ft Cleveland Cold Storage building on Broadway Avenue, built by Cleveland industrial developer Weston Inc. for family-owned Orlando Baking (about 330 employees in 2023) with a $2 million JobsOhio Ohio Site Inventory Program grant. The city's community benefits page lists the entity as Boron Orlando Baking Co., LLC - Weston, Inc., so Weston co-owns the vehicle.

Privately held Strongsville mortgage lender with 1,300+ employees in July 2020 and 1,590 plan participants in 2023; the Revitalization Grant supported reuse of a vacant Strongsville building as its headquarters with 450 new jobs promised. Company materials describe it as Strongsville-based but the fetched sources do not state where it was founded.

Urban Renewables II LLC is the brownfield redevelopment vehicle for the former Caraustar paperboard site in Rittman, taken over in 2012 by Ohio environmental firm Hull & Associates and its subsidiary, with John Hull listed as contact; Hull later merged into Verdantas (2,800 staff today). No grant-year headcount for Hull & Associates was found, so the bucket is a guess for a mid-size regional consultancy.

SFG Columbus Parsons LLC is the Stonemont subsidiary building the three-building, 859,240 sq ft speculative Castings Commerce Park on the former Buckeye Steel/Columbus Castings site at 2211 Parsons Avenue; Stonemont is an Atlanta industrial developer whose team page lists 96 people. The headcount is a 2026 website roster, not a 2023 figure.

parent: UGN, Inc. (joint venture of Autoneum Holding AG and Nihon Tokushu Toryo)
emp_source: Form 5500 participants 1,886 (2019) for sponsor UGN, Inc.; https://ugn.com/about/
notes: UGN is a Tinley Park, Illinois acoustic-parts maker formed in 1986 as a partnership of Nittoku (Japan) and what is now Autoneum (Switzerland); neither partner is treated as sole parent, and Autoneum alone has about 16,000 employees. Grants supported the Monroe, Ohio plant (opened 2015, 111-job expansion 2018).

Steris Corporation of Mentor is the US operating subsidiary of SEC registrant STERIS plc, which reported roughly 12,000-13,000 employees in its FY2016-FY2020 10-Ks; the parent was UK-domiciled from 2015 and Ireland-domiciled from 2019 after tax inversions, while executive operations stayed in Mentor. Founded in Ohio in 1985, so a reader may fairly call this an Ohio company with a foreign legal address.

Southgate Company LP is a partnership of Southgate Corporation, a Newark, Ohio industrial-park developer founded 1953, which received an OSIP grant for an 84,000 sq ft speculative building at 33 Innovation Park in Marysville (Nov 2020). The company publishes no headcount; the <100 bucket is a guess for a regional developer.

Alkermes Inc. (Wilmington plant) is the US subsidiary of Dublin-based SEC registrant Alkermes plc, whose 10-Ks report about 2,000-2,300 employees across 2017-2021; the EDGAR HQ state MA reflects the Waltham US base. Founded 1987 in Massachusetts.

emp_source: Form 5500 participants 105 (2019) and 108 (2023) for sponsor COTSWORKS, Inc.
notes: Highland Heights fiber-optic maker, an EDGAR Form D filer, with 105-108 plan participants and 73 jobs retained, so it sits at the line between <100 and 100-499. The company was acquired by Moog Inc. (NY) at a date not verified here, which may postdate the 2024 grant year.

emp_source: Form 5500 participants 4,912 (2023) for sponsor Otsuka America, Inc.; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Otsuka_Holdings
notes: Pharmavite (Nature Made) of West Hills, California has been owned by Tokyo-based Otsuka since 1989; its US plan is sponsored by Otsuka America with 4,912 participants and the Otsuka group employs tens of thousands worldwide. The grant supported the $200 million New Albany gummy plant begun in 2023.

parent: Bread Financial Holdings (formerly Alliance Data Systems)
notes: ADS Alliance Data Systems is the Columbus card-services unit of Alliance Data, renamed Bread Financial in 2022, whose 10-Ks show roughly 20,000 employees in 2017 and about 7,500 in 2022. Headquarters was Plano, Texas at the 2017 grant and moved to Columbus in 2019, so the OH label applies to the 2022 grant only.

emp_source: Form 5500 participants 5,320 (2019) and 8,048 (2023) for sponsor Belcan, LLC; https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belcan
notes: Cincinnati (Blue Ash) engineering services firm founded 1958 with about 10,000 employees, owned by private-equity firm AE Industrial Partners from 2015 until Cognizant bought it in August 2024, after the grant years. Resolved to the operating company per the PE rule.
